picks.d: One of the best free music festivals in the entire country takes over Golden Gate Park for three glorious days. Rilo Kiley, Alison Krauss, Robert Plant, Gillian Welch, Mavis Staples, Los Lobos — the lineup is genuinely absurd for a free event. Pack a blanket, pack snacks, and just go.

picks.t: Golden State Valkyries WNBA Playoffs — Game 3
picks.d: Series tied 1–1, winner takes all — this is the kind of game you'll be telling people you were at. The No. 2 seed Valkyries host the Dallas Wings in a win-or-go-home Game 3 at Chase Center. High-stakes, electric atmosphere, and women's basketball at its absolute best.

picks.t: RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me — Opening
picks.d: BTS's RM co-curates an exhibition with SFMOMA bringing together 200 works including Korean art never before shown in the US — it's a genuinely fascinating collision of pop culture and fine art. Member previews run Oct 1–3, then it opens to the public. This one's going to be a moment.

The #1 RA Pick for the Bay Area this week is a massive three-day weekender in Oakland with SHERELLE, Skee Mask, Objekt, Mala, Zenker Brothers, and a whole lot more. Indoor and outdoor programming, day into night — this is the dance music event of the season. Buy tickets now; it will sell out.

picks.t: My Morning Jacket — Seven-Night Fillmore Residency
picks.d: The Louisville rock legends kick off a seven-show residency at the Fillmore this Saturday and it is a big deal. MMJ is famous for marathon sets that wander through psychedelia, country, indie rock, and back again — and the Fillmore is the perfect room for it. Catch any night you can grab a ticket.

The 52nd annual Castro Street Fair is one of SF's most beloved community institutions — live performances, dancing, vendors, food, and the whole neighborhood out in full force around Castro and Market. Free, all-ages, and genuinely joyful. Show up and soak it in.

picks.t: Lucania — Grand Opening at the Ferry Building
picks.d: The Ferry Building's biggest vacant space has finally found its tenant: Lucania, from the team behind A16, focused on southern Italian cooking with a serious little-fish moment — anchovies, sardines, mussels. The 140-seat dog-friendly patio off Embarcadero Plaza is back, baby. This is the most anticipated restaurant opening of the fall.

picks.t: Terror vault: SLASHED — Return to Hellville
picks.d: Peaches Christ's theatrical haunted experience returns to the San Francisco Mint and it's bigger and more terrifying than ever. This is SF's premier haunted attraction — not your average jump-scare warehouse, but a full immersive theatrical production. Use code FUNCHEAP for $10 off tickets.

The Led Zeppelin frontman, one of the greatest rock vocalists to ever walk the earth, plays one of SF's most gorgeous historic theaters. This is a bucket-list show in a bucket-list room — the kind of night you replay in your head for years. One night only.

picks.t: The Menzingers + Hot Water Music + Weakened Friends
picks.d: This is a punk dream bill — three of the most emotionally resonant bands in the genre, all on one stage at the Great American Music Hall. The Menzingers are touring behind their new record and Hot Water Music are veterans in the best possible sense. If you have any emo or punk DNA in your body, do not skip this one.

picks.t: Exploratorium After Dark — Unplug and Play
picks.d: Adults-only evening at the Exploratorium on Pier 15 with interactive exhibits, live music, and a cash bar — it's like a science museum but make it a night out. Every After Dark has a different theme and this one is Unplug and Play. Perfect for a Thursday that feels like more than a Thursday.

picks.t: Night Garden on Third — Jazz Mafia Series
picks.d: While everyone migrates to Golden Gate Park, the People's Garden in Bayview is hosting three nights of intimate free music: Afrobeat Sunset Friday, Jazz Night Saturday, Soulful Sunset Sunday — all with Jazz Mafia. This is the hidden gem of the weekend, more neighborhood block party than festival.

picks.t: Gillian Welch & David Rawlings at the Fillmore
picks.d: One of Americana's most beloved duos — haunting harmonies, sparse guitar, timeless songs — at one of the best music venues on the planet. If you're not going to Hardly Strictly, this is where you go instead on Friday night. Deeply special.

picks.w: Sun Oct 4 – Mon Oct 12 · Mostly Free
picks.d: Fleet Week officially gets rolling this Sunday — the biggest event of its kind in the US — with ship tours starting Oct 6, the Parade of Ships on Oct 9, and the Air Show Oct 9–11. Free to watch from the waterfront, absolutely spectacular, and a true SF tradition. Block off next weekend too.

ongoing.t: Peter Pan Goes Wrong — SF Playhouse
ongoing.d: Hilarious physical comedy chaos running Tue–Sun through Nov 28 at 450 Post St.

ongoing.t: Ha Chong-Hyun Retrospective — Asian Art Museum
ongoing.d: Major Korean abstract painter, through January 25 — free first Sunday Oct 4.
Character Development, Alex Weinstein, and Flora + Fauna all running through October in Dogpatch.
Season wrapped in August — mark your calendar for next summer's free Sunday concerts.

new.name: Lucania
new.d: From the A16 team, focused on southern Italy with a beautiful little-fish section and a 140-seat dog-friendly patio finally bringing the Ferry Building's vacant space back to life.

new.name: Olive Juice
new.d: Warm neighborhood café in a converted paint store doing Mediterranean sandwiches, smoothies, yogurt, bread, and coffee — the anti-austerity wellness spot SF needed.

new.name: Shinka
new.d: Chef Fumio Yonezawa brings a modern Japanese-California concept to The Jay hotel with seasonal cocktails and omakase-influenced cooking.

new.name: Bayview Oyster Bar
new.d: Grilled and raw oysters, clam chowder, and Dungeness crab with garlic noodles from the chef behind the beloved Auntie April's — part of a great wave of new Bayview openings.

new.name: Monami
new.d: Upscale grill-it-yourself premium beef cuts in the old Noosh space on Fillmore, with both à la carte and tasting menus from the Ssal team.

new.name: Chicano Nuevo
new.d: The Infatuation called this $95 tasting menu one of the best things they ate in September — absolutely no skips on the menu.

classic.name: Bar Coto
classic.d: The Cotogna team's walk-in-only spot for coffee and sandwiches by day, cocktails and small plates by night — one of the best new additions to the neighborhood.

classic.name: Lorella Bakery & Café
classic.d: From the Octavia and Saturbake teams, so expect exceptional pastries alongside very good coffee on Polk Street.

classic.name: A16
classic.d: The OG that spawned Lucania — Neapolitan pizza, seasonal salads, and fresh pasta that have been making this neighborhood happy for years.

classic.name: Bar Part Time
classic.d: Late-night natural wine and dancing from the team behind the forthcoming Downtime — the Mission's best secret for a Tuesday that turns into a Friday.

classic.name: Rose Pizzeria
classic.d: Chronicle Top 100 #13 — nationally acclaimed Berkeley pizza that will soon be fueling the food menu at the Mission's Downtime bar.

classic.name: 15 Romolo
classic.d: The 115-year-old pseudo-speakeasy tucked down a North Beach alley reopens mid-October after a two-year renovation — get in before the crowds rediscover it.

bars.name: Paris 75
bars.d: French-inflected North Beach cocktail bar hosting the Singles Speed Dating + DJ Party this Friday — great atmosphere even on a regular night.

bars.name: Public Works SF
bars.d: Community-minded Mission club with a Funktion-One sound system hosting Mind Against all night long this Friday — one of SF's best dance rooms.

bars.name: 1015 Folsom
bars.d: 40 years as the center of SF nightlife — inclusive, diverse, forward-minded — with DJ Smokey and ilykimchi this Friday.

bars.name: Audio SF
bars.d: 250-capacity SoMa club with an eye to the future hosting Madota this Friday — one of the city's best rooms for discovering new electronic music.

bars.name: The Midway
bars.d: Massive Dogpatch event space and club hosting Elephante Saturday night — great for groups who want big-room energy with room to breathe.

bars.name: Rickshaw Stop
bars.d: Beloved neighborhood venue with Ecca Vandal Saturday and Stephen Dawes Wednesday — cozy, unpretentious, and reliably good.

bars.name: F8 / 1192 Folsom
bars.d: Home to NO BIAS × Trekkie Trax this Friday — a cross-cultural dance floor mixing Japanese hyper-pop and club sounds with SF underground energy.

bars.name: Bar Part Time
bars.d: The Mission's best late-night natural wine bar with a side of dancing — the team behind the forthcoming Downtime keeps this place electric.

games.teams: Valkyries vs. Dallas Wings — WNBA Playoffs Game 3
games.detail: Win-or-go-home Game 3 with the series tied 1–1. Must-see women's basketball.

sports.note: This is the highest-stakes game in SF this week — don't sleep on it.

games.teams: Warriors vs. LA Lakers — NBA Preseason
games.detail: Last home action before the regular season opens Oct 21. Great chance to see the squad without playoff pressure.

sports.note: Regular season home opener is Oct 23 vs. Memphis — mark it.
Regular season wrapped Sept 27. Check MLB.com to see if the Giants are in the postseason — World Series starts Oct 23.

concerts.d: The Led Zeppelin icon plays the grand and historic Orpheum Theatre for one night only. This is a genuine once-in-a-generation voice in a room that deserves it — if you're on the fence, get off the fence.
Two of Americana's finest — spare, haunting, and utterly transportive — at the Fillmore. A perfect counterpoint to the festival energy outside this weekend. Deeply special show.

West Coast storyteller-songwriter John Craigie brings his sharp wit and personal folk-rock to GAMH as part of the Hardly Strictly & GAMH 'Out of the Park' series. Tickets $40–$79.50 and worth every penny for fans of literate, funny, heartfelt songwriting.
Bay Area hip-hop and funk veteran and cornerstone of the local scene for decades. If you want to dance and feel deeply at home in SF on a Friday night, The Chapel is the move.

concerts.t: Igorrr with Secret Chiefs 3 & Violent Magic Orchestra
concerts.d: French avant-garde project blending baroque classical, black metal, breakcore, and operatic vocals — this is genuinely unlike anything else you'll see this year. Secret Chiefs 3 open. For the adventurous listener only, and absolutely worth it.
Sonoma County roots reggae with a jazz-infused, spiritual, conscious sound — the perfect Sunday wind-down after a big festival weekend. Tickets $30–$35.

concerts.t: The Menzingers with Hot Water Music & Weakened Friends
concerts.d: A punk dream bill: three of the most beloved bands in the genre, all anthemic and emotionally loaded. The Menzingers are touring behind 'Everything I Ever Saw' and this triple bill at GAMH is the kind of show you'll hear about for months if you miss it.

The British singer-songwriter behind the classic Rattlesnakes album does a rare solo electric set at The Chapel — literate, introspective, and intimate in the best way. A very special evening for anyone who knows his work.

One of Japan's biggest pop groups — formed on PRODUCE 101 Japan — brings polished choreography and a devoted global fanbase to the Warfield. If you know, you know; if you don't, prepare to be converted.

concerts.t: Thinking Fellers Union Local 282 with Bill Orcutt & Famous Mammals
concerts.d: SF experimental rock legends reuniting for rare performances alongside avant-guitar hero Bill Orcutt — a night of genuinely adventurous, left-field sound at GAMH. If you care about the deep history of SF's underground music scene, this is unmissable.

concertsOngoing.d: Seven-night residency with marathon sets — grab any night you can find a ticket.
Free monthly block party with live music curated by Carnaval SF lands Thursday Oct 8.

concertsOngoing.t: The Bends at Rickshaw Stop — Popscene Soundcheck
concertsOngoing.d: Popscene's reliable indie showcase with rising talent, Friday Oct 2.

concertsOngoing.t: Ecca Vandal with Speed of Light — Rickshaw Stop
concertsOngoing.d: Australian alt-pop mixing hip-hop, punk, and electro, Saturday Oct 3.

singles.d: Speed dating meets DJ night at Paris 75 in North Beach — one of the better cocktail bars in the city, which makes the whole thing feel a lot less awkward than a community center setup. Quick-fire dates, good drinks, and if nothing sparks, you're already at a great bar on a Friday night.

Fast-paced format designed for younger SF singles at Campus in the Marina — midweek dating that breaks up the grind in the best way. If you're in that age bracket and looking to actually meet people (not just swipe), this is worth the experiment.

For the SF singles who are done with situationships and actually want to meet someone with the same intent — this mixer at 316 Mason targets professionals looking for something real. Earnest, organized, and a genuinely refreshing alternative to bar-hop mingling.

singles.t: Slow Runners Club — Sunday Morning Run
singles.d: 2,300+ member run club that welcomes all paces, meets at the Panhandle, runs through Golden Gate Park, and ends with optional coffee. Post-HSB Sunday run through the park while the festival breaks down around you? Actually kind of perfect. You'll make actual friends here.

singles.t: Volo Glow Kickball + Flip Cup — Registration Open
singles.w: Register by Thu Oct 9 · League Starts Oct 15
singles.d: Thursday-night coed kickball under glow lights at Dolores Park with post-game bar meetups — Volo is genuinely one of the best ways to meet people in SF as a transplant or remote worker. Registration closes Oct 9 so this is your week to pull the trigger.

singles.t: SET: Mind Against — All Night Long at Public Works
singles.d: Not technically a singles event but honestly one of the best places to meet interesting people in SF — dancing at Public Works with a Funktion-One sound system and Mind Against playing the whole night. Show up alone, leave with a group. That's just how this venue works.

singlesOngoing.t: Run Club SF — Tue/Thu evenings at Kezar Stadium
singlesOngoing.d: Speedwork Thursdays and wildcard Tuesday runs with post-run social hangouts built in.
SF's longest-running indie dance night — still one of the best places to meet music people in the city.

date.title: Festival Love Story
date.tagline: Blanket, music, park — the classic SF first date.

steps.title: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass
steps.detail: Head to Golden Gate Park and find a good blanket spot near one of the stages. Bring snacks, share them — instant intimacy points. Alison Krauss, Gillian Welch, or Robert Plant depending on the day.

steps.title: Golden Gate Park Wander
steps.detail: After a few sets, take a walk through the park — Stow Lake, the Conservatory of Flowers, whatever direction feels right. Low pressure, gorgeous, free.

steps.title: Night Garden on Third (Fri–Sun)
steps.detail: Swing by the People's Garden in Bayview for Afrobeat, Jazz, or Soul with Jazz Mafia — intimate, local, and completely free. A side of SF most people never see.

date.title: Art + Oysters
date.tagline: Museums in the afternoon, little fish at dinner.

steps.title: RM x SFMOMA — Between You and Me
steps.detail: The new exhibition opened this week and it's a genuine conversation starter — 200 works, Korean art never shown in the US, co-curated by BTS's RM. Tickets ~$25.

steps.title: Walk the Embarcadero
steps.detail: From SFMOMA to the Ferry Building is a beautiful 15-minute walk along the water. Golden hour, Bay Bridge, the whole thing.

steps.title: Lucania at the Ferry Building
steps.detail: The brand-new restaurant from the A16 team just opened — southern Italian cooking with marinated anchovies, sardines, and mussels on the dog-friendly patio. Reserve early, this one's already buzzing.

date.title: Rock Royalty Night
date.tagline: Dress up, go out, see a legend.

steps.title: Dinner at Shinka
steps.detail: Japanese-California concept at The Jay hotel from Chef Fumio Yonezawa — seasonal cocktails and omakase-inspired cooking to set the tone for the evening.

steps.title: Robert Plant at the Orpheum
steps.detail: Friday Oct 2 — the Led Zeppelin frontman at one of SF's most beautiful historic theaters. One night only. This is the centerpiece of the evening and worth the splurge entirely on its own.

steps.title: Nightcap at 15 Romolo
steps.detail: The 115-year-old North Beach pseudo-speakeasy just reopened after two years of renovation. Down a small alley, great cocktails, very good energy. End the night right.

solo.title: Solo Festival Saturday
solo.tagline: Lose yourself in the crowd — in the best way.

steps.title: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass
steps.detail: Show up solo to Hardly Strictly and just wander between stages. No coordination required, no one to compromise with — this is the ideal solo festival experience.

steps.title: Golden Gate Park Stroll
steps.detail: Duck out of the crowds and take yourself on a quiet walk through the park. Recharge before round two.

steps.title: Free Rooftop Stargazing — SF State
steps.detail: Friday Oct 2 at 7 PM, SF State's free public stargazing with a giant telescope. Check weather-dependent updates before heading over. A surprisingly peaceful solo close to the day.

solo.title: Museum + Midweek Show
solo.tagline: Culture in the afternoon, punk rock at night.

steps.title: de Young Museum — Free Tuesday
steps.detail: First Tuesday of the month means free admission to the permanent galleries. American art, Pacific collections, and more — take your time, no agenda.

steps.title: Bar Coto for a Pre-Show Drink
steps.detail: Walk-in only bar and café from the Cotogna team in Jackson Square — great cocktails, good gelato, and the right vibe for solo pre-show time.

steps.title: The Menzingers + Hot Water Music at GAMH
steps.detail: Tuesday Oct 6 — solo show-going is underrated and GAMH is the perfect room for it. Doors at 6, lose yourself in the set, feel very alive.

solo.title: Adults-Only Thursday
solo.tagline: Science, cocktails, and a dance floor — treat yourself.

steps.title: Dinner at Lorella Bakery & Café
steps.detail: Early dinner at the new Russian Hill bakery-café from the Octavia and Saturbake teams. Exceptional pastries, great coffee, relaxed pre-evening energy.

steps.title: Exploratorium After Dark — Unplug and Play
steps.detail: Adults-only evening at Pier 15 with interactive exhibits, live music, and a cash bar. One of SF's most uniquely fun nights out. ~$20, 18+ only.

steps.title: JO1 at the Warfield
steps.detail: Thursday Oct 8 at 7:30 PM — catch the end of the night with one of Japan's biggest pop acts at one of SF's best mid-size venues. Polished, high-energy, genuinely fun.

birthday.title: Festival Birthday
birthday.tagline: The whole park is your party.

steps.title: Golden Gate Park Picnic Setup
steps.detail: Claim your spot at Hardly Strictly Bluegrass — assign someone to blanket duty, bring the birthday snacks and drinks, make it a proper setup.

steps.title: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass — Full Day
steps.detail: Rotate through stages, discover a new artist, watch an icon. The birthday person picks the sets. Alison Krauss, Mavis Staples, Los Lobos — take your pick.

steps.title: Castro Street Fair Wind-Down (Sunday)
steps.detail: If it's a Sunday birthday, pivot from the park to the Castro Street Fair for the last couple hours — dancing, vendors, and the whole neighborhood celebrating alongside you.

birthday.title: Haunted Birthday
birthday.tagline: October birthdays deserve a spooky night out.

steps.title: Dinner at Bayview Oyster Bar
steps.detail: New Orleans-style seafood in Bayview — grilled and raw oysters, clam chowder, Dungeness crab with garlic noodles. Festive, delicious, and supports a great new neighborhood spot.

steps.title: Terror Vault: SLASHED at the SF Mint
steps.detail: Peaches Christ's theatrical haunted experience is the perfect October birthday activity. Running nightly from 6 PM — use code FUNCHEAP for $10 off. Groups love this one.

steps.title: Nightcap at 1015 Folsom
steps.detail: DJ Smokey and ilykimchi on Friday Oct 2, or whatever's on when you finish. Forty years of SF nightlife history and the city's most inclusive dance floor. Happy birthday.

birthday.title: Legendary Birthday
birthday.tagline: Go big. You only turn this age once.

steps.title: Dinner at Monami
steps.detail: The new upscale Korean steakhouse on Fillmore — grill-it-yourself premium beef cuts, tasting menus, scallion pancakes. Perfect for a birthday group who wants an experience, not just a meal.

steps.title: My Morning Jacket at the Fillmore
steps.detail: Seven-night residency, Oct 3–11 — grab the birthday night and let MMJ play your soundtrack. Marathon sets, the Fillmore's legendary room, and a band at the absolute top of their game.

steps.title: The Midway — Elephante (Sat Oct 3)
steps.detail: If the birthday falls on Saturday, close out at The Midway in Dogpatch for Elephante's melodic house set. Multi-room, big sound, great for a group that wants to keep going.

friends.title: Classic SF Friend Day
friends.tagline: The kind of Saturday people move to SF for.

steps.title: Slow Runners Club — Panhandle
steps.detail: Sunday Oct 4 at 10 AM — meet at Baker & Oak and run through Golden Gate Park together. End with coffee nearby. All paces welcome, totally social.

steps.title: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass — Afternoon Sets
steps.detail: Walk straight from your run into the festival. Find a stage, find a spot, let the afternoon happen. This is peak SF.

steps.title: Castro Street Fair
steps.detail: Sunday Oct 4, 11 AM–6 PM — catch the last hour of the fair before it wraps. Dancing, vendors, live performances, and the whole neighborhood out. Free and joyful.

steps.title: Minnesota Street Project — Dogpatch
steps.detail: Multiple shows running: Character Development, Alex Weinstein, Flora + Fauna. Free galleries across multiple spaces — spend an hour wandering and letting people have opinions.

steps.title: RM x SFMOMA — Opens Oct 3
steps.detail: Head to SFMOMA for the big new exhibition — BTS's RM co-curating 200 works including never-before-shown Korean art. Great friend group conversation fodder.

steps.title: Bar Coto — Jackson Square
steps.detail: Walk-in-only bar from the Cotogna team for cocktails, small plates, and excellent gelato. The right place to debrief everything you just saw.

friends.title: Punk Rock Friend Night
friends.tagline: Dinner, then the most cathartic show of the week.

steps.title: Dinner at Chicano Nuevo — Bernal Heights
steps.detail: The $95 tasting menu with absolutely no skips — the Infatuation called it one of the best things they ate in September. Book the table, let the kitchen do the work.

steps.title: The Menzingers + Hot Water Music at GAMH
steps.detail: Tuesday Oct 6, doors at 6 — the punk dream bill of the year. Three beloved bands, one stage, one room that's built for exactly this kind of show. Sing every word.

steps.title: Bar Part Time — Mission
steps.detail: The late-night natural wine bar from the Downtime team for one last drink and maybe some dancing. The right way to close a very good Tuesday.

parents.title: Festival Family Day
parents.tagline: The kids will talk about this one.

steps.title: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass — Golden Gate Park
steps.detail: All-ages, free, and completely massive — set up the blanket early, let the kids roam, and enjoy music you actually want to listen to. Oct 2–4.

steps.title: Golden Gate Park Exploration
steps.detail: Between sets, take a family wander — Stow Lake, the buffalo paddock, the Dutch Windmill, the Conservatory of Flowers. There's genuinely no better free afternoon in SF.

steps.title: Castro Street Fair (Sunday Oct 4)
steps.detail: All-ages, 11 AM–6 PM — live performances, vendors, community organizations, and a joyful neighborhood energy that's great for families. A gentle, welcoming end to the day.

parents.title: Museum Day with the Fam
parents.tagline: Curious kids + curious parents = perfect Sunday.

steps.title: Asian Art Museum — Free First Sunday
steps.detail: Sunday Oct 4 is free first Sunday — Garuda in Bali and the Ha Chong-Hyun retrospective are both running. Kids love the objects and the scale; parents love the free part.

steps.title: Lunch at Lorella Bakery & Café — Russian Hill
steps.detail: New bakery from the Octavia and Saturbake teams — great pastries, good sandwiches, coffee, and a relaxed pace that works well with kids in tow.

steps.title: Disney Descendants & Zombies — Chase Center
steps.detail: Saturday Oct 3 at 7 PM — if you've got tweens or teens, this is the ticket. Live concert tour with the cast of Descendants and Zombies at Chase Center. They will lose their minds.

parents.title: Waterfront & Warfront
parents.tagline: Food, ships, and the kind of afternoon kids remember forever.

steps.title: Lucania — Lunch at the Ferry Building
steps.detail: The brand-new southern Italian restaurant from the A16 team just opened — dog-friendly patio, beautiful waterfront setting, great food. A genuinely special family lunch.

steps.title: Embarcadero Waterfront Walk
steps.detail: Walk the waterfront toward Pier 15 — the views, the water, the general magic of the Embarcadero on a sunny October afternoon. Stop at the Giant Sculpture Farewell Party if it's Friday Oct 2.

steps.title: Fleet Week Ship Tours Preview
steps.detail: Fleet Week runs Oct 4–12 with ship tours starting Oct 6 — plan ahead and book tours at the waterfront. Kids on a Navy vessel is an afternoon they will talk about for years. Mostly free.
